purpose: test whether explicitly oriented future noncommutativity at the endpoint carries chronology information that a symmetric first-order susceptibility probe missed
challenge_learning_rate_policy: exactly reuse the chronology-blind selected stage learning rate; no challenge-rate tuning

stage_randomness.rule: reset stage-specific seed on every stage-map invocation

candidate_state_model: K3 exact ordered-interaction prediction from the frozen spent-pilot basis
projection_direction: D_AB=I_AB(theta0)-I_BA(theta0), normalized by Euclidean norm; sign is fixed so D_AB has the same composition orientation as C_AB
direction_validation: directly recompute all six base C_AB(theta0) values and require agreement with D_AB before candidate or target decoding
primary_response_family: six signed normalized projections <C_AB(s),D_AB>/||D_AB|| in fixed challenge-pair order
reference_normalization: fit mean and nonzero coordinate scale from the 24 K3 candidate references only; never use target responses for normalization
decoder: nearest standardized K3 candidate response in Euclidean distance with stable tie order fixed by itertools.permutations(A,B,C,D)
target_geometry_role: descriptive diagnosis only; target-target geometry and minimum physical probe subset may not be used to choose features or tune the decoder
primary_support_rule: all five checks must pass; otherwise do not call the oriented probe successful and do not tune feature subsets on this output
if_primary_fails: record whether failure is intrinsic target-response collapse or K3 reference-model mismatch; do not expose confirmation codebooks
if_primary_passes: validate the smallest physical commutator subset and then freeze a finite behavioral continuation test before confirmation
